newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion says Australian share stabilises.
newsitem.headline: Lion says Australian share stabilises.

text.p: Australasian brewer Lion Nathan Ltd said on Monday its share of the Australian data from March suggested its share of the Australian beer market had stabilised.

"While annualised market share in Australia is 41.1 percent compared to 42.0 percent six months ago, March results indicate improved performance, particularly in New South Wales, and suggest that market share is stabilising," chief executive Douglas Myers said.

Myers said reorganisation of the Australian brewing business from five regional operations to a single streamlined business, under the direction of Gordon Cairns, had been completed and results were beginning to show.

Lion earlier reported a decline in February first half earnings to NZ$72.2 million from $91.44 million, in part reflecting a higher tax rate than last year, but mostly reflecting very competitive beer markets in Australia and New Zealand.

Lion's earnings from operations dipped 14 percent to NZ$181.5 million. Group revenue was NZ$1.34 billion, down 3.0 percent, but cash flow from operations was up 22 percent, reflecting improved capital management costs in Australia and lower interest costs.
Australian brewing earnings declined 10 percent to A$123.8 million of revenue of A$792.3 million.
New Zealand market share improved to 54.4 percent from 53.9 percent a year ago while earnings from domestic liquor operations fell to NZ$60.1 million from $68.3 million.

The soft drinks division made market share gains in both Australia and New Zealand but fierce competition depressed margins. Lion said it was working on a structural solution to the soft drinks business.
Myers said there were attractive growth prospects in China, where there company has an existing brewery at Wuxi and another under construction at Souzhou.
The company expects the China operations to make a profit contribution by 2000.
